T0601.title: OWASP Automated Threats
T0601.definition: An OWASP-defined classification framework for automated threats to web applications (OAT-001 through OAT-021), systematically categorizing automated abuse behaviors carried out against web applications by internet bots.
T0601.description: The OWASP Automated Threats to Web Applications project, maintained by OWASP, categorizes automated abuse behaviors against web applications into 21 classes (OAT-001 through OAT-021), each corresponding to a typical automated-threat pattern. Representative classes include OAT-007 Credential Stuffing, OAT-008 Credential Cracking, OAT-011 Scraping, OAT-014 Scalping, OAT-018 Vulnerability Scanning, and OAT-019 Credential Cracking. The framework provides a unified threat-classification language for the anti-scraping, anti-automation, and risk-control domains, facilitating cross-organization communication of threat intelligence and defense strategy. BREAK entities such as web scraping risk (R0027), process automation (R0001), and credential stuffing (R0032-001) all map to corresponding OAT classes. Whereas Bot Management (T0602) focuses on productized capability, OAT focuses on the threat-classification ontology itself.
T0601.usageExample: When analyzing a large-scale scraping incident, the risk-control team classifies it as OAT-011 Scraping under the OWASP Automated Threats (OAT) framework, then maps it to the corresponding web scraping risk (R0027) defenses.
